div.div: Why the second job exists. Static credentials outrank web identity in the AWS SDK's chain, so a drill running with static credentials proves nothing about the path a real failover takes — it would pass either way. Separating it is the only way the assertion means anything.

div.div: ⚠ client_id_list needs the standby SA's UNIQUE ID, not just sts.amazonaws.com. AWS matches a Google token on the authorized party (azp) as well as the audience, and for a GCE identity token azp is the service account's unique id. Every condition in the trust policy can match and STS still answers InvalidIdentityToken.

div.div: ⚠ The node's service account needs read on the MIRROR bucket, and it is easy to leave out: the CI drill's own identity reads that bucket constantly, so the mirror looks reachable while the identity that matters during an actual outage has never touched it. The standby could unseal a snapshot it had no permission to fetch.
